referrals.title: Victoria Barracks future use: Commonwealth feedback
referrals.body: Australian Government Department of Finance; Council publishes the local referral
referrals.purpose: Give community views and future-use suggestions about Victoria Barracks Sydney through the Defence Estate Audit divestment programme. Finance uses input with due diligence to prepare site-specific strategies.
referrals.method: Select Victoria Barracks Sydney in the NSW property list on the Department of Finance webform and provide feedback. This is voluntary community input, not a sale process or preference for a future buyer.
referrals.eligibility: Local communities, First Nations communities, site users, heritage and community groups, governments, industry and other interested stakeholders. Multiple sites may be selected.
referrals.disclosure: The form collects name, company, email, phone and comments. Finance may disclose information to Commonwealth agencies and contracted service providers for divestment strategies, with other use only by consent or legal authority. Do not provide unnecessary sensitive information or another person's information without their consent.

audits.coverageStatus: Partial discovery; current list incomplete
audits.summary: Rechecked all 30 first-page news entries covering February-September 2026, read relevant image-only statutory notices and recovered the live public Suggestions / Queries form and website privacy policy. One continuing input route is recorded; no dated current project invitation was confirmed in this bounded recent-source review.
audits.scope: Current project invitations, substantive planning/public-land notices and explicit continuing contribution methods. Existing standing Council procedures and named bodies remain separately listed. Routine house/shed applications, payments and procurement are not individually catalogued.
findings: The current generic Feedback page is a real suggestions/questions form, rather than a contact-only navigation page. Its CAPTCHA/delivery was not exercised.

The July differential-rates notice image contains a written submission route for electors and ratepayers, but its numeric closing date is 23 July 2026 at 4pm and is past. Its weekday says Wednesday while 23 July 2026 was Thursday; the conflict does not make the round current.
The August Plan for the Future notice records adoption on 26 August, limited to Corporate Business Plan changes from the annual budget, rather than a fresh public consultation.

The September Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee image says public attendance requires a requested electronic invitation for 22 September at 3.30pm. It is now a past meeting, and attendance is not evidence of a submission or current membership vacancy.
gaps: This bounded recovery reviewed the first 30 news entries and relevant image notices; older paginated news and the full external document library were not exhaustively re-enumerated.
The live feedback form uses legacy CAPTCHA code. Successful loading/delivery was not tested.
The general Council question-time source still refers to a 2025 calendar, as recorded in its existing pathway. Current question-policy conditions were not refreshed in this recovery.
No confirmed dated current project call in these sources is not evidence that no other channel or invitation exists.
closedExclusions: The September audit committee electronic meeting occurred 22 September 2026. The notice did not invite a present submission or standing committee membership.
The July differential-rates round closed in July 2026, with an inconsistent weekday in its printed deadline.
The May fees/charges notice reports an adopted resolution effective 1 July 2026 and contains no invitation for further response.
The August Council Plan adoption does not reopen consultation.
The 2023 Old Post Office survey promotion is historical and its directly linked form returns 404 on 8 November 2026; it is excluded as a current route.

audits.coverageStatus: Partial discovery; current list incomplete
audits.summary: Recovered the latest 60-page September-October newsletter and actual image-only contribution invitations. Current news and all 20 published-notice cards were rechecked; dated statutory hotel, rates and annual-electors notices were reconciled visually as closed or past. Two continuing community routes are recorded; the private-operator process is shown separately as a referral.
audits.scope: Current project invitations, substantive planning/public-land notices and explicit continuing contribution methods. Existing standing Council procedures and named bodies remain separately listed. Routine house/shed applications, payments and procurement are not individually catalogued.
findings: The latest newsletter explicitly renews its newsletter-improvement paper feedback invitation and Yalgoo Bush Fire Brigade membership invitation.

The image-only Golden Grove advertisement invites direct email project feedback now, with an early-2027 onsite consultative forum only proposed. Golden Grove Operations is responsible; Council publication is a referral, not Council or Traditional Owner endorsement.
The newsletter identifies 27 November and 18 December Council meetings at 10.30am, consistent with the separate existing calendar route; no duplicate meeting invitation was added.
gaps: This bounded recovery screened all 60 latest newsletter pages at overview size and read the actual contribution pages at full size; it did not re-read every fine-print third-party service advertisement.
The office-only brigade form and operator privacy terms remain unread. The operator's early-2027 forum has no exact published date or registration route.
Older news, separate planning records and every historical notice are not exhaustively re-audited. No claim that the three records exhaust all local participation is made.
closedExclusions: The annual electors meeting image confirms 31 July 2026 at 10am. It is a past meeting, not a forthcoming November invitation.

The current 10 June 2026 Hotel lease-disposal notice sought public submissions by 9am on 3 July 2026. This differs from the older operator recruitment advertisement, which closed 22 September 2025 at 4pm. Neither is open now.
The June 2026 differential-rates image sought elector/ratepayer submissions by 4pm on 3 July 2026, not an ongoing call.

Social activities, health appointments, school enrolments, service advertisements and retrospective event reports in the newsletter were screened separately from consultation. The announced training and health-service investigations do not themselves invite a current submission.
The 2024 train-lighting petition story and the 2024 SMS notification registration are not treated as current Council submission mechanisms.

referrals.title: Golden Grove renewable energy project: questions and feedback
referrals.body: 29Metals, Golden Grove Operations; referral published by Shire of Yalgoo
referrals.note: Comment on the operator's feasibility investigation for onsite solar, wind and battery storage and its potential effects on native flora, fauna and proposed locations. This is an operator-led referral advertised in the Council newsletter. Email questions, feedback or requests for information to the named Golden Grove Community Relations Advisor at jacqui.bradley@29metals.com, as invited on page 26. The operator also plans an onsite consultative forum in early 2027, but no fixed date, booking route or eligibility for that forum is yet published. Checked 2026-11-08.
referrals.scope: This is operator-led engagement advertised in a Council newsletter, separate from Council submissions. No closing date is published.
referrals.disclosure: The advertisement does not explain whether emails or names may be published, shared or retained. Operator privacy and subsequent statutory publication conditions were not reviewed.
